bibliographic.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
bibliographic.authors: Qingyun Wu, Gagan Bansal, Jieyu Zhang, Yiran Wu, Beibin Li, Erkang Zhu, Li Jiang, Xiaoyun Zhang, Shaokun Zhang, Jiale Liu, Ahmed Awadallah, Ryen W. White, Doug Burger, Chi Wang
bibliographic.citation_apa: Wu, Q., Bansal, G., Zhang, J., Wu, Y., Li, B., Zhu, E., Jiang, L., Zhang, X., Zhang, S., Liu, J., Awadallah, A., White, R. W., Burger, D., & Wang, C. (2023). AutoGen: Enabling next-gen LLM applications via multi-agent conversation. arXiv preprint arXiv:2308.08155.

methodology.study_design: open-source framework proposal with example application studies
methodology.technology_context: multi-agent LLM conversation framework (AutoGen) supporting LLMs, tools, humans, and flexible conversation patterns

eligibility.decision_rationale: The provided text describes AutoGen as a technical open-source framework for building LLM applications via customizable multi-agent conversations, including optional human inputs and flexible interaction patterns. It demonstrates effectiveness across diverse example domains (mathematics, coding, QA, operations research, online decision-making, entertainment), but the excerpt contains no explicit treatment of conversational governance, accountability, compliance, audit, risk control, or regulated high-stakes environments central to the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python metadata title was corrupted; full-text governance and regulated-domain relevance cannot be confirmed from the partial excerpt alone.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based only on front matter and partial introduction. The study clearly presents a framework objective and matching methodological approach, but sampling, ethics, limitations, and detailed empirical protocol are not visible in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: For the review question on conversational governance in regulated LLM systems, the available text offers coherent technical background on multi-agent conversation and human-in-the-loop support, but provides little or no direct evidence on governance mechanisms, oversight accountability, compliance, or regulated-domain deployment.

coding.subtheme: Flexible agent interaction patterns with optional human involvement
rq_alignment: technical enabler for conversational AI systems
partial alignment to human oversight via human-in-the-loop support

synthesis.main_claim: AutoGen is an open-source framework that lets developers build LLM applications through multiple customizable agents that converse with each other, and optionally with humans and tools, using flexible conversation patterns programmed in natural language or code.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a foundational technical framework and programming paradigm for multi-agent LLM conversations, with empirical demonstrations across varied non-regulated example applications.
synthesis.limitations: Provided excerpt does not document governance, compliance, auditability, safety controls, or regulated-domain evaluation; empirical sampling and limitations sections are not available in the supplied text.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence for multi-agent conversational architectures and human-in-the-loop integration, not as central evidence on conversational governance in regulated settings.
